lines.text: A subagent is a separate worker, with its own context, tools and instructions.
It does a side task and hands back only a summary.
Say a question means reading forty files.
In the main conversation, all forty would fill your context.
Hand it to a subagent, and it reads them in its own window,|then returns ten lines.
It starts fresh, without your conversation's history, so your context barely moves.
Claude Code ships with Explore, Plan, and a general-purpose agent.|Your own go in .claude/agents.
lines.say: Claude Code ships with Explore, Plan, and a general purpose agent. Your own go in dot claude slash agents.

lines.text: You can also ask for one directly:|use a subagent to find every place the config is read.
This portfolio has one called article writer.
It's a Markdown file with a description, the tools it may use,|and the house rules for every article: the structure, the tone, and the checks.
Its description says when to hand off, so the main agent knows when to call it.
Summaries lose detail, and you only see what it chose to report.
It also spends more tokens overall, because each subagent builds its own context.
It can't see what you've already read or decided, so give it a full brief.
So use one when a side task would flood the conversation, not by default.|The setup behind this series now defaults to the main session.
Codex supports custom agents too, defined in TOML.
lines.say: Codex supports custom agents too, defined in toml.
